leads.summary: Distinct desktop entries with the same display label share a launch deadline
leads.consequence: Launch desktop ID A, then a different desktop ID B with the same visible name at approximately 14 seconds while neither changes the active window or toplevel count. The comparison says sameApp, so B does not receive a new 15-second window. A's timer stops B's pending two-second delay at approximately 15 seconds, and B never shows its launch feedback. A plugin can also omit the name for two distinct desktop IDs, making both names the empty string. The open rename PR #10144 would let a user deliberately give two entries the same display label.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N2); Opus harness S6/S7

leads.summary: Two open launch-feedback PRs have assertions incompatible with this PR's current implementation
leads.location: test/shell.d/app-search-test.sh in open PRs #12966 and #11568; head shell/services/AppLibrary.qml:171,250
leads.consequence: If either PR #12966 or #11568 is integrated alongside #13095 while keeping its added test unchanged, the shell test suite fails even when launch feedback works. #12966 requires the exact text 'if (!launchTimeout.running) launchTimeout.start()' and absence of 'launchTimeout.restart()'; #13095 uses conditional restart. #11568 requires literal 'duration: 15000'; #13095 uses 'duration: launchTimeout.interval'. Both PRs also modify the same AppLibrary lines, requiring conflict resolution; reconcile the tests and select a single implementation before merging.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator read-only gh api (hunter-verify/), rechecked live by Opus in draft check

leads.summary: New source-text test fails to protect the assignment that makes sameApp work
leads.consequence: If the single root.launchName assignment at AppLibrary.qml:163 is removed, launchName remains its initial empty string, and every repeat launch with a nonempty name is classified as different, repeatedly resetting the launch timeout. All assertions in this new test still match unchanged source snippets, so the suite does not guard against a straightforward regression of its headline invariant. Add an assertion for updating launchName, preferably a behavioural sequence test rather than regex alone.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N3, mutant M5 executed); Opus plan-node-1 and plan-qml-3

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up on the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13095#issuecomment-5825753932) after [the author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13095#issuecomment-5833495355), checked at head `3d821e3`.

**Outcome:** both earlier findings are resolved at this head, and the test now guards the regression it was meant to catch. One statement in the earlier review was wrong and is corrected below. Four smaller notes follow.

| Earlier item | Status at `3d821e3` |
|---|---|
| Stuck toast not explained by `restart()` | **Resolved:** the launch OSD now has a finite duration, and the description says `Refs #12922`. One supporting claim is **withdrawn** (see the correction) |
| Different app launched near the first deadline loses its feedback | **Resolved** |
| Optional test improvement | **Resolved** |

**Verified:** in a QML model built from each revision's own `AppLibrary.qml` and `Osd.qml` code (stubbed toplevels and IPC delivery, see Test scope):

| Scenario | Base | Previous head | This head |
|---|---|---|---|
| `close` delivered before `show` | still up at the end of the 40 s run | still up at the end of the 40 s run | hides 15 s after it appears (about 17 s after the launch) |
| Same app launched at 0, 5, 10 s, no window | closes at 25 s | closes at 15 s | closes at 15 s |
| App A at 0 s, different app B at 14 s | B shown 16 s to 29 s | B never shown, closed at 15 s | B shown 16 s to 29 s |

The 15 s self-hide counts from when the toast appears, not from the launch deadline. In the reordered case after a same-app retrigger it can therefore last until about 15 s after the retrigger's toast. In normal delivery the timeout or a new window always closes the toast first. The stranding fix from 43c15a4015 is still intact, and the existing app-search and OSD tests pass at this head.

### Correction: the issue's reproduction does reach this code

The earlier review stated that the reproduction steps in #12922 do not reach `beginLaunchFeedback`, because the Files binding and `omarchy launch nautilus` run `bin/omarchy-launch-nautilus`. That was wrong:

- Step 1 of the issue also lists "the Files entry in the app menu". That entry runs `Menu.qml` `activateIndex` -> `appLibrary.launch` -> `beginLaunchFeedback`.
- The toast text the reporter quotes, "Launching Files…", is produced only by `beginLaunchFeedback` (at `v4.0.4` and at this head). `omarchy-launch-nautilus` shows no OSD.

So the reported toast came from this code path. The rest of that finding stands: at base, a toast that stays up longer than 15 s after the last launch still needs a `close` that never took effect, and the show/close ordering race remains a source-level explanation that has not been reproduced in a live shell.

**Impact:** the PR description repeats the incorrect reason ("The reporter's repro goes through `omarchy-launch-nautilus`, which does not use this code path").

**Suggested change:** update that sentence. `Refs` versus `Fixes` remains a call for the maintainers: the likely cause is now bounded rather than removed, and it is still unreproduced.

### "Same app" is keyed on the display name

`beginLaunchFeedback` receives only `name`, and `sameApp` compares display names. Two different desktop entries with the same Name (for example a native and a Flatpak build), or two plugin launches without a name (`PluginAppLibraryApi.launch` passes `""`), count as the same app:

```text
Model run, this head: two different entries both named "Files", no window yet
t=0    launch entry 1 -> timeout armed for t=15
t=14   launch entry 2 -> same name, timeout kept at t=15
t=15   timeout        -> feedback closed while entry 2 is still starting;
                         entry 2 never gets its own toast
```

**Impact:** feedback only, and only for name collisions within the 15 s window. It is the earlier different-app case in a narrower form.

**Suggested change:** `launch(desktopId, name)` already has the desktop ID. Passing it to `beginLaunchFeedback` and comparing IDs, while keeping the name for the toast text, matches the intent in the reply.

**Stale comment:** the comment on `launchOsdOpen` (`AppLibrary.qml` lines 29-31) still says the OSD "shows with duration 0, so only closeLaunchFeedback() takes it down".

**Optional test improvement:** two one-line regressions still pass every assertion in `app-library-launch-test.sh`. Deleting `root.launchName = String(name || "")` makes every named retrigger look like a different app, so the deadline moves again (launches at 0, 5 and 10 s close at 25 s, as on base). Moving that assignment above the `sameApp` comparison makes every launch look like the same app, which brings back the different-app case. Asserting that the assignment exists after the comparison would catch both. The message "self-hides at the launch deadline" also overstates the timing, since the 15 s starts when the toast appears.

**Related open PRs:** #12966 makes this PR's earlier timer change (`if (!launchTimeout.running) launchTimeout.start()`, as at `2a98d2c`, without the per-app restart), and its added `app-search-test.sh` assertions forbid any `launchTimeout.restart()` in `beginLaunchFeedback`, which this PR now uses on purpose for a different app. #11568 adds the same OSD duration backstop, and its test expects the literal `duration: 15000` rather than `launchTimeout.interval` (same value). Both edit the same `AppLibrary.qml` lines, so whichever change lands, the others would need reconciling.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of head `3d821e3`, previous head `2a98d2c` and base `28ceaae`, the upstream `v4.0.4` tag, qtdeclarative `QQmlTimer` source and Quickshell 0.3.1 `execDetached` and IPC handling. The PR's test ran in an isolated sandbox with Node against the head, the base, the previous head and labelled one-line variants. The timelines come from a QML model run with qml6 6.11.2 in core mode: verbatim launch-feedback and OSD code from each revision, with stubbed toplevels, stubbed IPC delivery (in order, or with `close` moved before `show`) and time scaled 1/5. No live shell or desktop session was used, and the show/close ordering race was not reproduced in a real shell. The related open PRs were compared by their file changes only.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
